definition: A team is a unit in the organisation's structure: a tree of units, each answerable to the one above (TAXONOMY.md D27). It carries work: projects, operations and data sources name the team whose work they are, and a programme names its lead team and supporting teams. That is also what decides who may edit what, since a contributor edits the work of their own teams and the teams beneath them. A team names its parent; the tree in Cartograph should be the one the organisation already keeps, and teams may be enrolled from the directory's groups. A team is not a person and holds no people (people are principals on the access list, never definitions), not a role (a role such as a sponsor or service owner is a Resource), not a beneficiary group (the people work reaches), and not a piece of work (a project or an operation names its team; a team is not made for one project).

/spec/parent.guide: The team this one sits under in the organisation's structure, if any. The top of the tree has none. Choose from the existing teams; when the team above is missing, define it first, top-down.

poor.text: quality-team, because the depot network team works with it every day
poor.why: Working together is not answering to: the parent is the team this one reports to, and joint work is shown by a programme's supporting teams.

poor.text: A team that sits beneath this one
poor.why: Makes a loop in the tree, so neither team sits above the other.

/metadata/name.guide: The team's name as the organisation uses it, so a person recognises it in a list or a directory.

poor.why: Names a person: Cartograph never names people, and the team outlasts whoever leads it.
Named for one project: a team is a standing unit, and the project names the team that carries it.

/spec/description.guide: What the team is responsible for, in one sentence: the work and services it carries, not who is in it.
good: Runs the fifteen depots, their cold stores and the collection rounds between them.
Keeps the registers and the seasonal reports the board and the members read.

poor.text: Three depot supervisors and a data analyst.
poor.why: Lists who is in it, not what it is responsible for; people and roles are kept elsewhere.
Says nothing a reader could use to tell whose work something is.
